checks.configuration: Dimension-512 Clifford tableau built deterministically from seed 409, inverted once and twice. Inverting a Clifford tableau is its symplectic conjugate transpose, so this drives the packed-bit-table transpose directly. Mirrors the upstream `simd_bit_table` suite (15 tests) and simd_bit_table.perf.cc.
checks.observable: the bit blocks of an inverted dimension-512 tableau, the double-inverse identity flag, and the column popcounts of the inverted x2x block

checks.configuration: Rotated surface-code memory-Z at distance 5 over 20 rounds with after_clifford_depolarization 0.002 and before_measure_flip_probability 0.002, generated by `stim gen`. 200,000 shots are sampled to a measurement record with `stim sample --seed 8675309`, then converted to detection events and observable flips with `stim m2d --append_observables`. 481 graded bits per shot (480 detectors plus 1 appended observable), probed exactly from stim rather than taken as ceil(n/8)*8 from the b8 width.
checks.observable: the mean, maximum and minimum of the per-bit detector-flip rates over all 481 graded bits, their spread, the per-shot event-count dispersion, and the fraction of shots carrying any event - six agreement invariants, each with its own bound

checks.configuration: Rotated surface-code memory-Z experiment generated by stim's own `gen` command at distance 11 over 100 rounds with after_clifford_depolarization 0.001, after_reset_flip_probability 0.001 and before_measure_flip_probability 0.001 - all three of the noise parameters upstream's fixture sets - then 1,000,000 shots sampled with `stim detect` (seed 12345), emitting detection events and observable flips in b8 format. 12,000 detectors and 1 observable, both probed exactly from stim rather than inferred from the b8 file size. Detection events are consumed from a pipe and never written. The fixture family is upstream's FrameSimulator_surface_code_rotated_memory_z_d11_r100_batch1024 in frame_simulator.perf.cc, scaled from 1024 shots to 1e6 so shots - the axis the bit-packed frame simulator parallelises over - is a real workload.
checks.observable: the mean, maximum and minimum of the per-detector firing rates over all 12,000 detectors, the spread across detectors, the per-shot event-count dispersion, and the raw undecoded observable parity - six agreement invariants, each with its own bound

checks.configuration: 4096-qubit Pauli strings drawn from a seeded numpy RNG (seed 211), multiplied 256 times in sequence. Graded through to_numpy() plus the sign and weight. Mirrors the upstream `pauli_string` and `PauliString` suites (36 tests) and the PauliString_multiplication_* perf benchmarks, which upstream measures at 6.8 us for 1M qubits.

checks.configuration: The repetition-code memory experiment from upstream's own getting-started notebook, generated by `stim gen --code repetition_code --task memory` at the notebook's distance 9 over 25 rounds with before_round_data_depolarization 0.04 and before_measure_flip_probability 0.01, then 200,000 shots sampled with `stim detect`. 208 detectors and 1 observable, both probed exactly from stim with a one-shot ASCII 01 sample rather than inferred from the b8 width. Detection events are consumed from a pipe and never written.
checks.observable: the mean, maximum and minimum of the per-detector firing rates over all 208 detectors, the spread across detectors, the per-shot event-count dispersion, and the raw undecoded observable parity - six agreement invariants, each with its own bound

checks.configuration: Dimension-1024 Clifford tableau built deterministically from seed 307, composed 8 times. At this dimension each operation is thousands of simd_bits word operations. Mirrors the upstream `simd_util` suite, whose 4 tests take 162 ms - the heaviest in mem/.
checks.observable: the bit blocks of a dimension-1024 composed tableau and the per-row popcounts of its x2x block

checks.configuration: Dimension-256 Clifford tableau built deterministically from seed 101, composed with itself 64 times, graded through Tableau.to_numpy(). Mirrors the upstream `tableau` suite (34 tests, 202 ms) and the tableau_random_* perf benchmarks.
checks.observable: the four x2x/x2z/z2x/z2z bit blocks and two sign vectors of a composed dimension-256 tableau, plus the inverse round-trip identity flag

checks.configuration: The two-detector X_ERROR circuit from upstream's own getting-started notebook, written out verbatim: H 0 / TICK / CX 0 1 / X_ERROR(p) 0 1 / TICK / M 0 1 / DETECTOR rec[-1] rec[-2]. The notebook samples it at 1e6 shots and prints the detector firing rate. Graded here over a sweep of three error probabilities - 0.05, 0.2 and 0.4, the notebook's own value being the middle one - at 1,000,000 shots each, with per-probability sampling streams spaced 1000 apart so no two initial conditions share one. One detector, probed exactly from stim rather than taken as ceil(1/8)*8, which would grade seven structurally-zero padding bits. Detection events are consumed from a pipe and never written.
checks.observable: the mean, maximum and minimum of the detector firing rate across the three error probabilities - three agreement invariants, each with its own bound

module.title: Bit-parallel stabilizer simulation: packed Pauli frames, tableau algebra and the SIMD word backends
excluded: src/stim/simulators/error_analyzer.* and dem/ - detector error model construction is graph work, not bit-parallel propagation; it is the other module
src/stim/simulators/graph_simulator.*, sparse_rev_frame_tracker.*, vector_simulator.* - auxiliary simulators outside the sampling hot path; left to the shared surface for now
hazards: INSTRUMENT SET. The three word backends are x86-only (-mavx2 / -msse2) and there is no NEON path, and CMakeLists.txt:25 tests CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR against a case-sensitive 'ARM64' that macOS's 'arm64' does not match, so on the packaging machine no machine flag is set at all and the portable bitword_64.h is what builds. Upstream's own reference times in stim_perf are 1.5-4x faster than this machine on the bit-parallel benchmarks. The incumbent must declare SIMD_WIDTH and host ISA explicitly or a port will be scored against a baseline 1.5-4x slower than Stim at speed.

Sampling is stochastic: shot outcomes depend on an RNG stream, so any check that samples must either seed and accept that a port's stream will differ, or grade statistical invariants. Deterministic sub-paths exist and are preferable where available - tableau algebra, stabilizers_to_tableau, and reference sampling are all deterministic.

simd_bits_not_zero_100K reports 310 ps against a 32 ns upstream reference, which is not a credible hundredfold speedup and suggests the compiler elides the loop. Do not build a graded workload on that benchmark without checking what it executes.
module.expensive_path: Bit-parallel propagation of packed Pauli frames: every Clifford gate is a handful of XOR and popcount operations across simd_bits words, with shots packed along the word axis, and the whole thing runs through the bitword abstraction in src/stim/mem/. Measured with upstream's own stim_perf: FrameSimulator_depolarize1_100Kqubits_1Ksamples 8.1 ms, FrameSimulator_surface_code_rotated_memory_z_d11_r100_batch1024 7.8 ms, DemSampler_surface_code_..._1024stripes 38 ms, and on the tableau side tableau_iter_all_3q 140 ms, tableau_iter_unsigned_3q 95 ms, stabilizers_to_tableau_576 62 ms, tableau_random_1000 61 ms. The micro-benchmarks underneath are the primitives every one of those calls: simd_bits_xor_10K 6.5 ns, PauliString_multiplication_1M 6.8 us, CliffordString_multiplication_10K 460 ns.
